audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Camille Levels 3, 4-5 and first item and gave Aurora Level 1, which is close to the inverse of both the page's own whys and the win rate. The matchup was also graded TRICKY at 7.5/10 difficulty while Aurora wins it.
audit.why: whys[0] says "Level 1 is even"; whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Aurora winning — "start chipping her down", "you out-trade her up close", "you control spacing and zone her off CS", "zones her engage", "force the all-in now" — and only whys[6] hands the lane over. 55% over 60 games backs an Aurora-favoured lane, so TRICKY / 7.5-10 / orange tone contradicted the data on the same page.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Camille, and the grade moved from TRICKY 7.5/10 to FAV 4/10 with the matching tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named Aurora's ultimate "Between the Worlds" — no such ability — and gave no cooldown for either ultimate, so the 6 spike had no timing attached.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140/120/100 and The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90. At rank 1 they are the same 140 seconds, which is why level 6 is a stand-off rather than a kill window for either side: whoever burns it into a fight they do not close is down an ultimate for over two minutes.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (140s) zones her all-in and The Hextech Ultimatum is also 140s — whoever wastes it is down for two minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot is described only as "her engage/stun" with no mention that it needs a wall, and Tactical Sweep — the ability that actually funds her lane — is never mentioned at all. Adaptive Defenses is missing too.
audit.why: Hookshot (E, 16/15/14/13/12, 800): "Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing." No wall, no engage — so where you stand in the lane decides whether she has an all-in at all. Tactical Sweep (W, 15/14/13/12/11, 610): "Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille" — the near half does none of that, so stepping in rather than back denies her the slow, the bonus damage and the heal in one move. Adaptive Defenses (P) shields her against the damage type of the attacker, so her first auto on you gives her a magic shield sized off her max health — that is the burst window that keeps disappearing. Precision Protocol (Q, 9/8/7/6/5) is an auto reset whose recast does significantly more damage if she waits between the two attacks, so the pause after her first empowered auto is the tell.
audit.corrected: Tactical Sweep slows and heals her only in its outer half — stand close and it does neither.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Track Hookshot" appeared eleven times with no cooldown and no condition.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 and requires terrain. Both halves matter: the number tells you how long the punish window lasts, the terrain requirement tells you where it exists at all.
audit.corrected: Hookshot needs a wall to pull to (16s) — in open lane it is dead.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization line says "his healing fights your pattern" without naming what heals her.
audit.why: Tactical Sweep's outer half is her only heal in lane, and it is the reason Grievous Wounds timing matters here. Naming it converts a generic anti-heal note into a positioning rule.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — Tactical Sweep's outer half heals her.

notes: champ-data/_kits/_missing/aurora.json asserts two things about The Hextech Ultimatum that Riot's own description does not support — that Camille goes untargetable during it, and that it is a channel Between Worlds can cancel. Riot's text is only "Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area" plus bonus magic damage on her attacks. Both are derived-flag artefacts, so I did not put either on the page; logged in unverified. The anti-heal itemization line lives at report[8].t. Boots are listed as Sorcerer's Shoes against a fully physical-damage Camille; that looks wrong but boot choice is a build call, not a fact from the kits, so I flagged it rather than editing it.
